course_name_original: Materials for Energy Conversion and Storage
course_name_en: Materials for Energy Conversion and Storage

learning_outcomes.text: Provide a comprehensive view of the materials and fundamental principles underlying energy storage and energy conversion technologies.

Cover fundamentals of electrochemical systems such as supercapacitors, batteries, fuel cells, electrolysis-based e-fuels, and photoelectrochemical conversion devices focusing on their operating principles, material requirements, performance limitations, and recent breakthroughs.

Focus on energy conversion mechanisms for energy harvesting, including light energy conversion (photovoltaic technologies), mechanical energy conversion (piezoelectric and triboelectric materials), and thermal energy conversion (thermoelectric and thermionic effects).
Emphasize the link between materials, physical principles, and device performance, supported by exercise sessions that apply the concepts to real energy systems.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to physical concepts in electrochemistry
Electrode/electrolyte interface: energetic treatment and equilibrium
Theory of charge transfer over electrode/electrolyte interface
Specifics for tortuous and porous electrodes
Principles and materials science aspects of batteries
Next generation batteries: Conversion materials, metal-air batteries
Interface engineering and interphase control for battery performance
Green hydrogen and e-fuels as energy carrier

assessment_methods.method: Oral exam during the examination period with open questions

institution: KU Leuven - Faculty of Engineering Science
degree: Bachelor in de ingenieurswetenschappen (Bachelor of Engineering Science, Leuven)
